lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Show with a model that 1/3 = 2/6. Shade both.

FEEDBACK
A thirds bar with one third shaded matches a sixths bar with two sixths shaded on the same length.

WATCH FOR
Changing only the denominator without matching shaded amount does not create an equivalent fraction.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Build eight equivalent pairs using area or length models (include halves/quarters/eighths and thirds/sixths). Write the equality and a sentence about equal shaded amounts.

Write a short reflection naming one step you corrected and why.

WORKED MODEL

teach_steps.explain:
Equivalent fractions name the same amount of the same whole using different equal-part sizes (for example 1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8).

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner choose methods based on place value, quantity and accurate working, rather than guessing digits by shape alone. Keep every step justified.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the places, values or distances that carry the method. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your working with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your reasoning? If a digit or place is uncertain, identify what would have to be regrouped or counted again. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: Changing only the denominator without matching shaded amount does not create an equivalent fraction. Correct the value or method, not just the appearance of the digits.
